chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abu Ali, from al-Yasa' al-Qummi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I intend to do something and seek God's guidance (istikhara) for it, but my opinion is not confirmed in it; should I do it or leave it?' He said: 'Look, when you stand for prayer, for indeed the devil is furthest from the person when he stands for prayer. So look at something that occurs to your heart, and take it. And open the Quran (Mushaf) and look at the first thing you see in it, and take it, if God wills.'

key_terms.الاسْتِخَارَة: Seeking guidance or choice from God

ai.seo_question: What is the method of Istikhara when one's mind is still confused after praying?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a specific form of Istikhara (divine guidance) where the believer seeks clarity through intuition during prayer or by randomly selecting a Quranic verse (Istikhara bi-l-Quran). This method reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of combining spiritual introspection with reliance on the Divine Word, emphasizing that the heart's inclination during the state of humility in Salah is a key indicator of divine will.
